data.narrative:
Lightmatter is a Series C chip design company that has raised $420M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 3 public semiconductors peers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private-stage frontier chip companies including Tenstorrent, Positron AI, and DEEPX.

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression modeling uses the $420M raised as a proxy base and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement, yielding $714M. Peer-median anchoring samples three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies—DEEPX ($529M, Series C), Positron AI ($1.0B, Series B), and Tenstorrent ($2.7B, Series D)—producing a median valuation of $1.0B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiple (20.5x median across the three public names) is not applicable due to absence of disclosed revenue.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $607M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $857M. The range width reflects heterogeneity in peer stage and valuation outcomes rather than fundamental uncertainty about the company itself. Key unknowns limiting precision include undisclosed revenue, unit economics, and customer concentration—standard constraints for pre-revenue or early-revenue chip ventures at this stage.
